title: AMD MI400 will market memory bandwidth over peak FLOPS at Advancing AI
body: When AMD takes the stage at Advancing AI 2026 on July 22-23 at Moscone Center, expect the MI400 pitch to lead with memory rather than raw compute. The generational story reporting points to is a bandwidth jump of more than 2x over MI350, built on CDNA 5 and TSMC's 2nm node, with the rack-scale 'Helios' system and the availability timelines held back at the 2025 preview finally detailed. The framing matters because the binding constraint in inference has shifted: long-context workloads inflate KV-cache footprints, so buyers increasingly value larger HBM pools and smarter parallelism over headline FLOPS. That same logic explains NVIDIA's counter-positioning, with Blackwell Ultra GB300 reaching 288GB of HBM3e and Rubin Ultra variants targeting 512GB. With HBM capacity reportedly sold out through calendar 2026 and TAM projected near $100B by 2028, the top of the accelerator market is settling into a memory-capacity and bandwidth contest, and AMD's July reveal is the near-term catalyst that makes that reframing explicit.

reasoning.because: Reporting on MI400 leads with >2x MI350 memory bandwidth, not peak FLOPS gains
reasoning.given: Long-context inference inflates KV-cache; HBM sold out through 2026 makes capacity the constraint
reasoning.so_that: Vendors market memory bandwidth/HBM capacity as the headline spec, reframing the accelerator race
reasoning.landing: AMD frames MI400 around memory at Advancing AI, July 22-23, 2026 (Q3 2026)
reasoning.plain_language: AMD's new AI chip will brag about memory speed, not raw power, when it's shown off July 22-23.

summary: At Advancing AI on July 22-23, 2026, AMD is expected to position the MI400 primarily around a >2x memory-bandwidth gain over MI350 rather than peak compute. Long-context inference inflating KV-cache and HBM sold out through 2026 make memory the binding constraint, mirrored by NVIDIA's 288GB-to-512GB HBM roadmap. The top of the accelerator market is becoming a memory-capacity and bandwidth contest.
